chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man forgot the Tawaf al-Nisa' (the final circumambulation) until he had intercourse with his wife.
He (peace be upon him) said: Women are not permissible for him until he visits the House (performs Tawaf al-Nisa').
And he (peace be upon him) said: He should be ordered to have it performed on his behalf, if he does not perform Hajj again.
But if he dies before Tawaf is performed on his behalf, then his guardian or someone else should perform it on his behalf.

key_terms.دَخَلَ أَهْلَهُ: Had sexual intercourse with his wife
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: The final circumambulation of the Kaaba performed at the conclusion of Hajj
key_terms.يَزُورَ الْبَيْتَ: Visits the House (Kaaba), referring to performing Tawaf
key_terms.يُقْضَى عَنْهُ: Performed on his behalf (as a substitute)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man forgets Tawaf al-Nisa' before intercourse?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of sexual intercourse stems specifically from the omission of Tawaf al-Nisa', distinguishing it from the general state of Ihram restrictions. The hadith establishes a practical mechanism for fulfillment, allowing for proxy performance (Qada) by the heir or another individual if the pilgrim dies or is unable to return, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the flexibility of ritual obligations. This highlights the juristic principle that the barrier to intimacy is lifted once the specific missed pillar is compensated, ensuring the Hajj is considered complete.
